logline: London detectives unearth decades-old remains and unravel the interconnected secrets of seemingly ordinary people, in a cold-case drama where the moral damage of buried truth is as devastating as any active crime.

renewal.note: Renewed for Series 7 in February 2025. DCI Jessie James (Sinead Keenan) continues alongside DI Sunny Khan (Sanjeev Bhaskar) following the departure of Nicola Walker's character at the end of Series 4.

bollymeter.basis: 73% on Rotten Tomatoes (11 critics). Metacritic score of 78 (23 critics). Critics praised Chris Lang's structurally disciplined writing and the multi-stranded format that made four suspects' lives genuinely worth inhabiting.

pull_quotes.text: Every action, every plot development felt organic, emerging inevitably from character and circumstance, not laziness.

seasons.review_body: Unforgotten launched on ITV in October 2015 with a structural formula that distinguished it from procedural convention: human remains are found, a cold case opens, and the investigation draws in four or five suspects whose present lives are carefully established before the past dismantles them. Chris Lang's writing was disciplined in ways critics quickly noticed - the discipline James Donaghy described in the Guardian as every development emerging organically from character rather than plot convenience. Nicola Walker's DCI Cassie Stuart and Sanjeev Bhaskar's DI Sunny Khan formed a partnership of unusual warmth and intelligence. The Metacritic score of 78 reflected a consensus that the series was serious, emotionally intelligent British crime drama in the best tradition. The 73 percent Rotten Tomatoes score was lower than later seasons would achieve, suggesting the format's pleasures were not immediately obvious to all critics.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes (7 critics). The series' creative peak, according to critical consensus. Lang's writing and Walker's performance reached their highest register. Alison Graham called it 'so much more than a murder-of-the-week' in Radio Times.

pull_quotes.text: Unforgotten is so much more than a satisfying murder mystery. It is such a human show.
Chris Lang's thoughtful thriller is so much more than a murder-of-the-week.

seasons.review_body: Series 2 achieved a 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score and is widely regarded as the series at its peak. The cold case format operated with maximum efficiency: a new victim, new suspects, new secrets accumulated over decades. Critics in multiple outlets converged on the same virtues - the compassion extended to characters who have done terrible things, the refusal of easy moral resolution, the quality of the writing at the level of individual scene and exchange. Walker and Bhaskar's partnership had by now achieved the comfortable authority of long-established television detectives, and the emotional climax of Series 2 generated the kind of reaction from audiences and critics alike that the best crime drama earns. Alison Graham in Radio Times described the finale as 'a haunting and moving episode, an essay in the corrosive power of secrets.'
seasons.season_over_season: Series 2 refines the formula to near-perfection; the case mechanics and the suspects' parallel stories achieve complete integration.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes. Three consecutive BAFTA-nominated seasons. Critics praised the sustained quality and the structural confidence with which Lang constructed another set of morally compromised suspects.

seasons.review_body: Series 3 maintained the 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score, earning consecutive BAFTA nominations alongside the two preceding series. The format was now operating with assured confidence: Lang had identified exactly how many suspects could be viably sustained across six episodes, how much personal backstory was required to make the moral reckoning land, and how the cold case investigation should be paced relative to the present-day consequences. Unforgotten had established itself as arguably the most consistent drama on British television. Walker and Bhaskar's chemistry was the emotional constant, and the series demonstrated that a formula rigorously applied could be a strength rather than a limitation.
seasons.season_over_season: Series 3 confirms that the format is a genuine strength - the consistency of execution is itself the achievement.

bollymeter.basis: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes (14 critics). Mike Hale in the New York Times called the Walker-Bhaskar partnership 'reason enough to watch.' David Zurawik of the Baltimore Sun called it 'even more compelling' than the three preceding BAFTA-winning seasons. The finale is among the most discussed episodes in the series' run.

pull_quotes.text: The relaxed and intimate teamwork of Walker and Bhaskar is reason enough to watch Unforgotten.
It is even more compelling than the three BAFTA Award-winning seasons that preceded it.

seasons.review_body: Series 4 aired in February 2021 and drew the strongest critical response since Series 2. Mike Hale in the New York Times singled out Walker and Bhaskar's partnership as sufficient reason to watch regardless of the case. David Zurawik in the Baltimore Sun called it the best series yet. The finale generated immediate conversation about its treatment of consequence, and the ending of Cassie Stuart's character arc became one of the most talked-about moments in British television drama of the year. The 93 percent Rotten Tomatoes score across 14 critics reflected a critical consensus that Series 4 was not merely sustained quality but active reinvention of the format's emotional possibilities.
seasons.season_over_season: Series 4 raises the emotional stakes to their highest point and the finale delivers on that ambition entirely.

bollymeter.basis: Sinead Keenan replaced Nicola Walker as lead. Critics acknowledged the difficult task of succeeding Walker and generally found Keenan's DCI Jessie James a credible successor, though comparisons were inevitable.

seasons.review_body: Series 5 faced the structural challenge of rebuilding around a new lead following the Series 4 finale. Sinead Keenan's DCI Jessie James arrived with a different register to Walker's Cassie Stuart - more abrasive, more emotionally defended - and critics were broadly supportive of the recalibration. Sanjeev Bhaskar's Sunny Khan provided continuity and the cold case format operated with its accustomed structural discipline. The series was a qualified success: proof that Unforgotten could survive the loss of its founding lead, even if the particular alchemy of Walker and Bhaskar could not be replicated. Audiences largely followed.
seasons.season_over_season: Series 5 is essentially a new show with inherited architecture; Keenan earns the trust placed in her without quite reaching Walker's register.

bollymeter.basis: Series 6 continued the Keenan-led era with the format operating reliably. The cold case and the suspects' interlocking secrets delivered the expected pleasures. ITV renewed for Series 7 in February 2025.

seasons.review_body: Series 6 aired in February 2025 and ITV's simultaneous announcement of Series 7 confirmed the show's continued health as a schedule cornerstone. Keenan and Bhaskar's partnership had by now settled into its own comfort, distinct from but no longer measured exclusively against the Walker era. The cold case format - new victim, new suspects, new secrets - continued to provide the structural clarity that distinguishes Unforgotten from more melodramatic crime drama. Critical coverage acknowledged a well-made series delivering its established pleasures reliably, without the urgency that had attended the earlier landmark seasons.
seasons.season_over_season: Series 6 consolidates the post-Walker era; the Keenan-Bhaskar partnership is now established on its own terms.
